items.title: 52300_Trummy Young oral history interview
items.q: And then he had another guy, Roger Segur. He had another guy Bud Estees.

ctx.x: Zilner used to write for Louis years ago, you know. And he'd do a few things for Earl. It's just like Lunceford's band. Lunceford had quite a few -- Lunceford had quite a few arrangers at -- in that band that -- that wrote for that band and never played with him, you know. People -- one of the best arrangers we had was William -- Billy Moore -- William Moore, Junior. He went to Europe years ago. But he wrote things like "What's your story, Morning Glory" and those things for Lunceford's band.

Nobody -- if you mention Billy Moore -- William Moore, nobody know who it was. But we knew. And then he had another guy, Roger Segur. He had another guy Bud Estees. Don Redman used to write for Lunceford. See, all these people that you never knew. You'd say oh, that's the Lunceford sound. But that's not so. That was a lot of different arrangers were writing for that band. Anybody who made a good arrangement.
Eddie Durham did a lot of good arrangements for Lunceford's band. But you don't hear those names associated with Lunceford. All you hear is Sy Oliver and Eddie Wilcox, you know.
